events.title: Virginia Ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: Virginia became the tenth state to ratify the Constitution, after a fierce debate in which Federalists agreed to recommend adding a Bill of Rights.
events.significance: Virginia's approval pushed the Constitution past the nine-state threshold and strengthened the new federal government. It also helped build momentum for the Bill of Rights.

events.title: Battle of the Little Bighorn Begins
events.description: Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer led the U.S. 7th Cavalry against a large force of Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors in Montana. Custer and the men under his immediate command were wiped out.
events.significance: The battle was a famous Native American victory, but it brought a harsh U.S. military response. It is remembered as a defining clash of the Plains Wars.

events.title: North Korea Invades South Korea
events.description: At dawn, North Korean forces crossed the 38th Parallel and invaded South Korea. They quickly captured the capital, Seoul.
events.significance: The invasion started the Korean War, a major early Cold War conflict. It drew in the United States, the United Nations and China, and the peninsula remains divided today.

events.title: Croatia and Slovenia Declare Independence
events.description: The parliaments of Croatia and Slovenia proclaimed independence from Yugoslavia, in a day of landmark declarations.
events.significance: The declarations accelerated the breakup of Yugoslavia. Slovenia's separation was relatively brief, while Croatia's led to a prolonged and bloody war.

events.title: Michael Jackson Dies
events.description: The 'King of Pop' died of cardiac arrest in Los Angeles at the age of 50.
events.significance: His sudden death prompted a global outpouring of grief. It also marked the end of one of the most influential careers in popular music.
